newsitem.title: USA: CBOT TRADERS SAY USDA DATA BULLISH FOR CORN.
newsitem.headline: CBOT TRADERS SAY USDA DATA BULLISH FOR CORN.

text.p: CBOT traders said U.S. crop production estimates issued early Tuesday by USDA were bullish corn but bearish for soybeans and wheat.
Corn futures were called to open up five cents to their 12-cent limit. Soybeans and wheat were expected to open around three to five cents lower.

"I think we're going to be sharply higher, limit up on the corn," said Don Roose, president of U.S. Commodities. "The weather (recent rains) will help corn some but it's not going to help it a great deal."

USDA estimated this year's U.S. corn crop at 9.276 billion bushels, sharply below the average estimate in a Reuter survey of analysts of 9.554 billion. The total is slightly below last year's crop of 9.293 billion.
The U.S. soybean crop was forecast at a record 2.744 billion versus an average analysts' forecast of 2.680 billion and last year's 2.382 billion.
"Corn takes a front seat initially (CBOT open) and we might be limit up on corn," said Steve Bruce of E.D. and F. Man International. "The bean number is going to be even bigger on the next report."
USDA put U.S. wheat production at 2.531 billion bushels, up from an average analysts' estimate of 2.476 billion and last year's crop of 2.282 billion.
Most traders expected wheat to open lower on the bearish production data although there was some talk it may hold its own or even open higher aided by spillover from an expected surge in corn prices.

"The (wheat) crop is significantly above the average guesses but the carryout projections went from 650 (million bushels) to 695," said Dan Cekander, analyst with FIMAT Futures. "That's just a small increase in the carryout."
Cekander pointed out that USDA had cut its wheat production estimates for key competitors in the export market.
USDA cut its estimate for this year's Canadian wheat crop to 23.50 million tonnes from a previous estimate of 25.50 million and Australia's crop to 16.00 million tonnes from 18.50 million.
